ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, square $ABCD$ has a side length of $2$. Points $E$ and $F$ are two moving points on side $AD$, satisfying $AE=DF$. Lines $BE$ and $CF$ are drawn, and $BE$ intersects the diagonal $AC$ at point $G$. Line $DG$ is drawn and intersects $CF$ at point $H$. When line $BH$ is drawn, what is the minimum value of $BH$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, \\
since square ABCD, it follows that $AB=CD$, $\angle BAE=\angle CDF=90^\circ$ thus $\triangle ABE \cong \triangle DCF$ (SAS), hence $\angle ABE=\angle DCF$. Since the median line where AC is located is the axis of symmetry of the square, it follows that $\angle ABE=\angle ADG=\angle DCF$. Since $\angle ADG + \angle GDC = 90^\circ$, it implies $\angle DCF + \angle GDC = 90^\circ$, hence $\angle DHC = 90^\circ$ which means $DH \perp CF$. Therefore, point H moves on the circle with CD as its diameter. When point H moves to the midpoint of AC, BH is the shortest. Connect BD and intercept AC at point O, since $BH + DH \geq BD$, when points B, H, and D are on the same line, since the perpendicular segment is the shortest, hence when BH $\perp$ AC, that is, when point H coincides with point O, the value of BH is minimum. In right $\triangle BOC$, $BO=BC\sin\angle BCO=2\times \sin45^\circ=2\times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}=\sqrt{2}$. Therefore, the minimum value of BH is $\boxed{\sqrt{2}}$.

method.method_draft: Synthetic locus route. First read the diagram as a square with A top-left, B bottom-left, C bottom-right, D top-right; E and F lie on the top side AD, BE meets diagonal AC at G, and line DG meets CF at H. From the text use AB=BC=CD=DA=2 and AE=DF. Prove triangle ABE is congruent to triangle DCF by SAS: AB=CD, AE=DF, and both included angles are right angles. Hence angle ABE equals angle DCF. Since AC is the symmetry axis of the square and G lies on AC and BE, reflecting line BE across AC gives line DG, so angle ABE equals angle ADG. Therefore angle ADG equals angle DCF. Because AD is perpendicular to CD, angle ADG plus angle GDC is 90 degrees, so angle DCF plus angle GDC is 90 degrees; with H on DG and CF, this gives angle DHC=90 degrees. Thus H lies on the circle with CD as diameter. As E and F move through the allowed positions on AD, the relevant locus is the arc from D toward the midpoint O of AC, with the limiting position E=D, F=A giving H=O. On this arc the distance from B is minimized at O; equivalently O is where H lies on diagonal BD closest in the permitted locus. Since O is the center of the square and half of diagonal BD, BH=BO=(2sqrt(2))/2=sqrt(2).

method.method_draft: Coordinate/algebra route. Read the diagram as A top-left, B bottom-left, C bottom-right, D top-right, with AD horizontal and E,F on AD. From the text, set the square side length to 2 and let t=AE=DF, with 0<=t<=2. Assign coordinates B=(0,0), C=(2,0), A=(0,2), D=(2,2). Then E=(t,2) and F=(2-t,2). The diagonal AC has equation x+y=2. Line BE intersects AC at G, giving G=(2t/(t+2), 4/(t+2)). The line through D and G has equation y-2=(t/2)(x-2), while line CF has equation y=(2/t)(2-x), with endpoint cases handled by continuity. Solving these two equations gives H=(2(t^2-2t+4)/(t^2+4), 8/(t^2+4)). Therefore BH^2=x_H^2+y_H^2. raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, square $ABCD$ has a side length of $2$. Points $E$ and $F$ are two moving points on side $AD$, satisfying $AE=DF$. Lines $BE$ and $CF$ are drawn, and $BE$ intersects the diagonal $AC$ at point $G$. Line $DG$ is drawn and intersects $CF$ at point $H$. When line $BH$ is drawn, what is the minimum value of $BH$?
raw_record.answer: \textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, since square $ABCD$, it follows that $AB=CD$, $\angle BAE=\angle CDF=90^\circ$ thus $\triangle ABE \cong \triangle DCF$ (SAS), hence $\angle ABE=\angle DCF$. Since the diagonal $AC$ is an axis of symmetry of the square, it follows that $\angle ABE=\angle ADG=\angle DCF$. Since $\angle ADG + \angle GDC = 90^\circ$, it implies $\angle DCF + \angle GDC = 90^\circ$, hence $\angle DHC = 90^\circ$, which means $DH \perp CF$. Therefore, point $H$ moves on the circle with $CD$ as its diameter. When point $H$ moves to the midpoint of $AC$, $BH$ is the shortest. Connect $BD$ and let it intersect $AC$ at point $O$; since $BH + DH \geq BD$, when points $B$, $H$, and $D$ are on the same line, and since the perpendicular segment is the shortest, when $BH \perp AC$, that is, when point $H$ coincides with point $O$, the value of $BH$ is minimum. In right $\triangle BOC$, $BO=BC\sin\angle BCO=2\times \sin45^\circ=2\times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}=\sqrt{2}$. Therefore, the minimum value of $BH$ is $\boxed{\sqrt{2}}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a square ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right; E, F are on the upper side AD, and E is on the left side of F; diagonal AC is drawn, segment BE intersects AC at G, after connecting DG it intersects CF at H, and finally BH is considered. Reasoning: The side length of the square is 2, so AB=CD=2, and ∠BAE=∠CDF=90°. Also because AE=DF, △ABE and △DCF are congruent by SAS, obtaining ∠ABE=∠DCF. Diagonal AC is the axis of symmetry of this square; under reflection, B maps to D, and G remains unchanged on AC, therefore line BE reflects to line DG, so ∠ABE=∠ADG. Thus ∠ADG=∠DCF. Also AD⊥CD, so ∠ADG+∠GDC=90°, hence ∠DCF+∠GDC=90°, that is, DG⊥CF, therefore ∠DHC=90°. By the inscribed angle theorem, H lies on the circle with CD as diameter. As E, F move on AD and satisfy AE=DF, H moves on the corresponding arc in the figure from D to the center O of the square, that is, the intersection point of AC and BD; when E=D, F=A, G=O and H=O. The point on this arc closest to B is O, so the minimum value of BH is BO. The side length of the square is 2, BD=2√2, and O is the midpoint of BD, therefore BO=√2. Hence the minimum value of BH is √2.
